analyses.title: Persistent features across SAE widths
inputs: Upstream: 18 full-corpus SAEs; original embeddings/activation caches for candidate discovery
analyses.method: Independently solve maximum-cardinality matching on each full-source graph, then intersect matched source IDs across all larger widths. Signed cosine or Pearson >=0.7. Use ascending feature IDs, sorted CSR and SciPy 1.15.3 for deterministic tie-breaking. Decoder graphs are exhaustive; Pearson persistence is exact for this rule on retained graphs, with no lower-bound guarantee relative to exhaustive independent intersections. Check all 32 counts and selected IDs; optionally reconstruct 72 Pearson graphs.
analyses.command:
python paper.py plan persistence --config /path/to/resources.json
python paper.py run persistence --config /path/to/resources.json
analyses.gap: Full streaming candidate discovery requires corpus activation caches.

analyses.title: Cross-distribution decoder matching
inputs: Upstream: full/wiki/no-wiki/random1/random2 SAEs, KMeans centroids, and PCA components
analyses.method: Solve maximum-cardinality matching on 60 pair graphs and check 120 directional proportions. Similarity >=0.7 is signed cosine for SAEs/KMeans and absolute cosine for PCA. Divide by the source dictionary size; PCA has embedding-dimension width.
analyses.command:
python paper.py plan split-directions --config /path/to/resources.json
python paper.py run split-directions --config /path/to/resources.json
analyses.gap: Baseline weights and the original graph-construction caches are not included in the models bundle; graph optima are independently recomputed.

analyses.title: Ground-truth hierarchy recovery
inputs: evaluation: ordered rows, splits, embeddings and target memberships; models: 18 full-corpus SAEs
analyses.method: Reaggregate 72 saved fits into 90 cells, pooling category-model trajectories. Feature/threshold selection uses training rows only; test F1 uses held-out rows. Positive thresholds predict activation >= threshold. GBIF eligibility counts source species and common-name labels union their species memberships.
analyses.command:
python paper.py plan main-numbers --config /path/to/resources.json
python paper.py run main-numbers --config /path/to/resources.json
analyses.gap: The compact command reaggregates saved fits. The hierarchy-probes workflow refits all 72 dataset/model/width combinations from sparse activations; encode/probe supports individual fits from exported model inputs.

analyses.title: Parent and child a-prefix recovery
inputs: Wordfreq Gemini probe summary.tsv files across nine widths (included in results)
Original per-width sparse activation caches (not bundled; regenerable from embeddings and models)
analyses.method: Upper panel: held-out F1 for the a-prefix and eligible two-letter children, selecting each detector separately. Lower panel: fix the training-selected a detector at each width and compute recall by prefix on all 200,000 words, including training and test rows.
analyses.command:
python paper.py plan prefix-example --config /path/to/resources.json
python paper.py run prefix-example --config /path/to/resources.json
analyses.gap: Run prefix-recall before prefix-example to recompute recall. The original hierarchy sparse cache format differs from the CSR NPZ written by the package encode command.

analyses.title: Computed containment graph and curated Food/Music examples
inputs: Gemini 131K post-TopK activation cache on 89,827,558 rows
full_experiments/results/gemini_131k_hierarchical_families/: selections, edges, text examples and labels
analyses.method: Active means >0.05. Require child/coactivation support >=100, parent support > child support, 95% Wilson lower containment >=0.70, reverse containment <=0.50, lift >=5; remove shortcuts with a qualifying two-edge path. The 114,762 retained pairs form the computed graph. Humans select and label 33 features/32 edges per displayed hierarchy; the compact table retains all 66 features/64 edges.
analyses.command:
python paper.py plan compact-hierarchies --config /path/to/resources.json
python paper.py run compact-hierarchies --config /path/to/resources.json
analyses.gap: Supply graph caches, saved selections, and labels. Use path_aliases to resolve recorded resource locations.

analyses.title: Training corpus, sparsities, seeds and budgets
inputs: Original checkpoint configs and 1,852 shard metadata/header records
Nine control recipes generated with --include-controls; original and control checkpoints remain external.
analyses.method: Tables are authored LaTeX checked against recorded provenance. Gemini has 89,827,558 rows in 929 shards; Nemotron has 89,227,558 in 923. MIRACL title/text are separate prepared collections. PAQ samples 10M records with seed 42 and emits questions and answers. One-million-step budgets except Gemini 131K (two million, auxiliary coefficient 1). The control table records all nine fixed-k/alternate-seed checkpoints with full SHA-256 identities, seeds and budgets.
analyses.command:
python paper.py script --config /path/to/resources.json -- scripts/generate_model_configs.py --include-controls
python paper.py script --config /path/to/resources.json -- tools/inventory_training_data.py --output /path/to/training-shards.json
analyses.gap: Metadata hashes identify shard descriptions, not dense tensor contents. Training-state continuation requires compatible optimizer and RNG states.

analyses.title: Hierarchy datasets, labels and saved splits
paper: Appendix: P3 dataset counts and splits
analyses.method: Rows, ordering, and original train/test labels are preserved. Country and continent question datasets are distinct from bare city-name inputs. Category filtering removes targets, not rows. GBIF common-name targets use unions of source species memberships.
analyses.command: Inspect evaluation/datasets.json; use atomic-features encode and probe as documented in REPRODUCTION.md.
analyses.gap: Embedding regeneration requires the specified providers and preprocessing settings.

analyses.title: Strict exclusive persistence
analyses.method: Require a signed-cosine edge strictly >0.7 with no other above-threshold partner at either endpoint, in every larger dictionary. This is a different statistic and threshold convention from Figure 2a.
analyses.command:
python paper.py plan exclusive-persistence --config /path/to/resources.json
python paper.py run exclusive-persistence --config /path/to/resources.json

analyses.title: Persistence sensitivity to cosine/Pearson thresholds
inputs: Original decoder checkpoints and cross-width retained Pearson neighbors/manifests
analyses.method: Independently match each full-source graph and intersect matched source IDs at thresholds 0.5, 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8. Decoder edges are exhaustive signed cosine; Pearson uses retained candidates. Independent intersections need not be monotone in the threshold and candidate intersections are not certified lower bounds.
analyses.command:
python paper.py plan thresholds --config /path/to/resources.json
python paper.py run thresholds --config /path/to/resources.json
analyses.gap: The threshold sweep requires candidate arrays, graph manifests, and reference caches for each threshold.

analyses.title: Alternative exclusive cross-distribution matching
inputs: Full/wiki/no-wiki/random1/random2 SAE and PCA dictionaries for each embedding model
analyses.method: Exclusive edges use similarity > 0.7 and degree one at both endpoints. SAE cosine is signed; PCA cosine is absolute for admission and competitors. PCA maximum and exclusive proportions are identical on these saved graphs; the maximum is 15.0716%.
analyses.command:
python paper.py plan split-directions --config /path/to/resources.json
python paper.py run split-directions --config /path/to/resources.json
analyses.gap: Requires baseline dictionaries and exclusive-match caches.

analyses.title: Cross-distribution activation matching
inputs: 16K SAE activations on each displayed row distribution
analyses.method: Each heatmap row fixes the evaluation distribution for both SAEs. Use fresh 512-dimensional CountSketch, 32 candidate neighbors per direction, full-row Pearson rescoring, top-five retention, and exact maximum-cardinality matching at signed Pearson >=0.7. Counts are candidate-graph lower bounds.
analyses.command:
python paper.py plan split-activations --config /path/to/resources.json
python paper.py run split-activations --config /path/to/resources.json
analyses.gap: The compact candidates bundle contains cross-width neighbors, not these distribution-specific split neighbors.

analyses.title: Synthetic prefix recovery under width, frequency and sparsity variation
inputs: Upstream: 468 trajectories, 11 milestones, original synthetic model/evaluation files
analyses.method: Final budget 1,024,000,000 examples, three paired seeds, generating sparsity K=8. Sample fixed-size supports with probabilities proportional to products of rank weights. Geometric recovery uses cosine >=0.9; activation recovery uses separate validation/test streams and injective assignment at F1 >=0.8. Prefixes permit 10% misses; hierarchical units are three atoms per complete family. Plot prefix atoms/SAE width; bands are seed ranges, not confidence intervals.
analyses.command:
python paper.py plan synthetic-recovery --config /path/to/resources.json
python paper.py run synthetic-recovery --config /path/to/resources.json
analyses.gap: Replotting requires saved numerical CSVs; training and evaluation require all 468 trajectories and their milestone checkpoints.

analyses.title: Persistence across learned synthetic SAEs
inputs: 78 groups of six final checkpoints; shared 400,000-row held-out streams per group
analyses.method: Independent full-source pairwise maximum matchings followed by intersection of matched source IDs on exhaustive signed cosine and continuous-activation Pearson graphs at >=0.8. Normalize by every source coordinate, including inactive ones. This measures learned-SAE persistence and does not impose ground-truth recovery, family completeness, or a prefix miss allowance.
analyses.command:
python paper.py plan synthetic-persistence --config /path/to/resources.json
python paper.py run synthetic-persistence --config /path/to/resources.json
analyses.gap: Reporting also verifies graph optima and compares the 0.7 baseline. Both thresholds’ graph/checkpoint provenance trees are required and are not in the compact bundles.
